ops.title: VM runtime assessment 2026-07: keep tart; PVG overhead = display sleep, not resolution
ops.body:
# VM runtime assessment (2026-07-14)

**Verdict: keep tart.** Every macOS-capable alternative (lume, macosvm) sits on the same Virtualization.framework with identical overhead; the lighter runtimes (vfkit, krunkit, Apple `container`) cannot run macOS guests; nobody implements the VZ memory balloon (tart, lume, UTM — UTM#4136 open), so static right-sizing is the only RAM lever; XNU's 2-concurrent-macOS-guest cap binds regardless of wrapper. tart is now `openai/tart` (Cirrus Labs acquired 2026-04) — more investment, not less. A swap would churn `scripts/lib/launchd.sh write_agent()`, `yclaw/vm.py`, `remote.py`, the manifest, tests, and packer for zero win. (hermes-on-Apple-`container` is a separate rearchitecture — see the spike memo note of the same date: NO-GO for production now, prototype-able.)

**PVG (`ParavirtualizedGraphicsGPUTask`) facts + measurements:**
- One live host-side Metal-renderer XPC task per running VM; tart attaches the graphics device unconditionally (`--no-graphics` only skips the window). Orphans (~3 MB) leak from a framework teardown bug sometimes (VirtualBuddy #616) but not always — metal's clusters cleaned up on VM stop twice on 2026-07-14; host reboot reaps orphans; no safe automated reap (can't distinguish orphan from live without XPC introspection).
- Live-task CPU is driven by guest frame-submission rate, not framebuffer size: 1024x768 awake mean 16.7% of a core vs 800x600 awake mean 21.1% (no reduction), both 27-32 min post-boot on metal. Fresh boots run 15-25%; the ~2% Activity-Monitor figure is a multi-day decayed average.
- **Guest display sleep is the lever**: `pmset -a displaysleep 1` → the task flatlines at 0.0% (frame submission stops). Codified for metal in `darwin/metal.nix` (commit fbbd937a); system sleep stays hard-off. Applies to metal ONLY — bluebubbles' display does real VNC-automation work; hermes has no compositor.
- Fleet sizing after the shrink: metal 2 vCPU / 8 GiB / 800x600 (wired cap auto-tracks to 2048 MB — piecewise formula), hermes 4 / 4 GiB, bluebubbles 2 / 4 GiB.
